Let's use our new-found knowledge to further study the career of Serena Williams. First, let's attach the packages we need: 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
```

Second, let's import and wrangle the data (sort of) like we did in Exercise 01. This will give us the finals where Serena participated. We'll call the dataset `serena_finals_data`.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
serena_finals_data  <-
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gruggeri/tennis_wta/master/wta_grand_slam_data.csv" %>% 
  read_csv(col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>% 
  select(year, winner_name,loser_name, tourney_name,round) %>% 
  filter(
    winner_name == "Serena Williams" | loser_name == "Serena Williams",
    round=="F"
    ) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))
```

Now let's create a new column where we'll declare whether Serena won or lost in a given match. For this, we'll use a new function: `case_when()`, which assigns values that fulfill a logical condition. The syntax goes roughly like this:  

```r
case_when(condition ~ value_to_assign)
```

- Inspect the results of the following chunk of code:

```{r}
serena_finals_data %>% 
  mutate(
    won_or_lost = 
      case_when(
        winner_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Won! :)",
        loser_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Lost! :("
        )
    )
```
Now let's use `group_by()` and `summarise()` to break down:

- How many times did Serena won or lost the tournaments? 

```{r}
serena_finals_data %>% 
  mutate(
    won_or_lost = 
      case_when(
        winner_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Won!",
        loser_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Lost!"
        )
    ) %>% 
  group_by(won_or_lost) %>% 
  summarise(number_of_championships = n())


```

- How many times did Serena win the tournament per year? 

```{r}
serena_finals_data %>% 
  mutate(
    won_or_lost = 
      case_when(
        winner_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Won! :)",
        loser_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Lost! :("
        )
    ) %>% 
  group_by(year, won_or_lost) %>% 
  summarise(number_of_championships = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

- How many times did Serena win the tournament per tournament? 

```{r}
serena_finals_data %>% 
  mutate(
    won_or_lost = 
      case_when(
        winner_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Won! :)",
        loser_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Lost! :("
        )
    ) %>% 
  group_by(tourney_name, won_or_lost) %>% 
  summarise(number_of_championships = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()
```
